title: Epictetus

author: Epictetus
pd_statement: The Discourses of Epictetus were written down by his pupil Arrian in the second century; the Encheiridion, or Manual, is Arrian’s summary of the teaching. This edition follows A Selection from the Discourses of Epictetus with the Encheiridion in the English translation by George Long (1800–1879), which is in the public domain. Long’s wording and his words in round brackets are kept; his Greek terms in brackets are left out, and the key terms are explained in the glossary. Obvious printing errors are corrected.

headline: Some things are yours.
Others are not.
Know the difference.
paras: Born a slave, lamed in body, banished from Rome by an emperor, Epictetus became the most practical teacher of the Stoic school. His lessons, written down by his pupil Arrian, have guided soldiers, statesmen and ordinary readers for nearly two thousand years.

This beautifully designed annotated edition presents George Long’s classic selection from the Discourses and the complete Enchiridion, and adds what today’s reader needs: a clear guide to Stoic ideas, a plain-language note and a small practice for every discourse and chapter, and a guided 30-day practice.
